findings.title: A string-reflective production constructor root vanishes from the census and is not refused
findings.source: source_bindings.py constructor_census (a call is a root only if its callee resolves to TARGETS or its spelling ends in a target class name); constructor_graph.prove (never compares the current production rows with the frozen census); use_sites.audited_nodes/REFLECTION (protected only by Name resolution; sys.modules subscripts, operator.attrgetter, importlib are not audited).
findings.counterexample: tools/lan_pilot.py only: line 9 'import argparse' -> 'import argparse, operator' (no line shift) and :3945 -> observer = operator.attrgetter('ObservationWorker')(sys.modules['inv.observer_worker'])(state, NodeTLSClient(**tls(args.state))). All names bound (state is the local dict), fresh AST valid, lan_pilot witnesses (runtime 902-903 helper, Database constructor) resolve with recorded hashes. Owner provenance() ACCEPTS with 5 production rows and classDbInputUnions all ['inv.db.Database']; the same with runtime(state) also leaves only 5 rows (reviewer-bound-counterexamples-result.json).
findings.impact: The derived census can lose a real production root without refusal, which is what 'unknown must remain unresolved, never force closed' forbids. Actual 72028 sources contain no attrgetter/methodcaller/importlib/sys.modules/getattr_static forms (grep over the 10 core/root files), so the actual closure is unaffected.
findings.minimalFix: Refuse when any frozen production census row is missing or changed in the current census (UNRESOLVED:CONSTRUCTOR_ROOT_REMOVED_OR_HIDDEN), and add sys.modules subscripts, importlib.*, operator.attrgetter/methodcaller, inspect.getattr_static/getmembers and string constants naming protected classes/modules/fields in a new context to the audited reflection set. Add the bound counterexample (state and runtime(state) variants) as span-preserving negatives with producer sanity.

findings.title: Owner objects bound by For targets or by non-protected factory results escape to foreign callables
findings.source: use_sites.py INSTANCE_NAMES and audited_nodes (instance names are a fixed set plus Assign targets of protected-prefix calls; For/With/comprehension targets and results of tracked forwarding factories such as inv.workspace_config.configured_workspace are never audited; Attribute loads are audited only when rooted at self).
findings.counterexample: workspace_config.py inside 'for runtime in pool.values():' add 'from foreign_module import register_runtime' + register_runtime(runtime) | register_runtime(runtime.db) | register_runtime(runtime.db.transaction); app.py after 'workspace = configured_workspace(...)' add 'from foreign_module import register_workspace' + register_workspace(workspace) | register_workspace(workspace.runtime.db). All 5 ACCEPT through the owner pipeline with bound names, fresh AST and producer sanity (constructor witness workspace_config:47 / app Database site resolve). Controls refuse: runtime.db = ..., workspace.runtime.db = ..., register_runtime(result.runtime), foreign(worker), foreign(db.transaction).
findings.impact: L1 asked that every load of a proven owner/root db outside recorded contexts, including callable-method escapes, BLOCK. The pool values are the RestrictedWorkspaceRuntime instances whose self.db feeds NodeObservation (workspace_api:98); foreign code receiving them can rebind db or install an observer after construction, outside the analyzed files. Actual 72028 has no such escape statements and no external .db/.observer/statement_observer/placement_metric_sink writes anywhere (reviewer git grep), so the actual closure is unaffected.
findings.minimalFix: Propagate instance-ness: names bound by For/With/comprehension targets whose iterable or context mentions an audited instance or owner, and Assign targets whose value is a call to a tracked forwarding function or an attribute/subscript of an audited instance, join the audited set; the frozen-context diff then refuses new escapes. Add the five bound counterexamples as negatives.

constructor_graph.environment is flow-insensitive (last Assign before the line wins) and ignores With/For/except/match binding forms. Reviewer: 'with foreign_context() as db' or 'for db in (foreign_database,)' before observer_worker:58 -> graph ACCEPT, full provenance REFUSE via use-site INSTANCE:db. Sound today only because every actual constructor argument is an audited instance name or a helper call; keep the graph/use-site dependency explicit or make the graph refuse untracked binding forms.

The model's tenant gate is keyed by (tenantId, epoch), while actual inv.tenant_controls has no epoch. add_node uses setdefault, so a node added under a new epoch would get a fresh unstopped gate. Unreachable now (control_epoch is fixed and scope epoch must equal it); key by tenant only if an epoch writer is ever modelled.
